title: signal-harvest-and-prospectivity-catalog-for-model-mismatch-detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, repeatable playbook and telemetry catalog that captures 'model mismatch' signals from customer workloads, competitor model changes, and public model releases, and synthesize those signals into a prioritized prospectivity catalog for PM/GTN teams.

Why this matters: Customers choose Redwood based on predictable latency, fallbacks, and model availability. When competitor models change (latency/cost/features) or open models introduce behavioral regressions, we need an early-warning triangulation mechanism to 1) surface actionable model substitutions, 2) quantify enterprise risk for Reserved/Dedicated customers, and 3) feed provisioning/procurement triggers.

Scope:
- Define 12 canonical mismatch signals (e.g., embedding drift, tokenization oddities, hallucination spike, latency step-change, quality delta on enterprise evaluation sets, new API contract incompatibilities).
- Instrument signal collection for hosted and dedicated traffic (sampling, anonymized metadata, eval-set re-runs).
- Build a triage rubric that maps signals to prospectivity actions (monitor, field probe, urgent vendor outreach, autoscale/fallback policy change).
- Produce a first 30-customer pilot run with synthesis report and recommended provisioning triggers.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Catalog of 12 signals with detection rules and thresholds documented.
- Pilot with 30 customers (or equivalent traffic slice) producing at least 18 prioritized prospectivity items.
- Time-to-detect: median detection within 24h of a material model change for high-impact signals.
- Decision-to-action pipeline: at least 70% of high-impact signals produce a concrete next step recorded in the playbook (e.g., schedule canary, change routing policy).

Acceptance criteria:
- Detection rules validated on historical incidents (at least 3) and produce expected flags.
- Playbook includes ownership mapping (PM/Eng/DS), notification patterns, and runbook links.
- Exportable CSV/JSON catalog for Sales/Customer Success with standardized fields (impact, confidence, suggested action).

Risks & trade-offs:
- Privacy: need to balance signal fidelity with PII / customer data. Approach: focus on anonymized metrics, aggregated deltas, and behavioral fingerprints rather than raw customer content.
- Noise vs. sensitivity: initial thresholds may produce false positives; plan for iterative threshold tuning and human-in-the-loop confirmation step.
- Engineering cost: MVP will rely on sampling + offline re-run rather than full production hooks to limit infra lift.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.com/confluence/display/MLO/Signal+Harvest+Playbook (doc draft)
- Draft schema & CSV template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SignalCatalogTemplate
- Prototype notebook for detection rules: https://github.com/redwood-inference/signal-hub/pulls/47 (PR: draft alerting rules)

Primary stakeholders: Product (Aisha), Applied ML (Dr. Mei Chen), Runtime Eng (Samir Khan), Observability (Lina Gomez), Solutions/SE (Ravi Malhotra).

Planned phases:
1) Definition (2 weeks): finalize signals, thresholds, pilot customer selection.
2) Instrumentation MVP (3-4 weeks): sampling pipelines, offline re-run harness, synthetic tests.
3) Pilot run (2 weeks): run against pilot customers, iterate thresholds.
4) Hand-off & packaging (1 week): CSV outputs, Sales/CS brief, runbook.

Notes on prioritization: Focus first on signals that (a) directly impact costs/latency SLAs for Dedicated customers and (b) are detectable with low engineering lift. Examples: sudden tail-latency increase for a single model variant; embedding cosine shift > 0.15 vs. baseline for two enterprise eval-sets.

Next steps (short-term):
- Sync with Applied ML to finalize the 12 signal definitions (meeting scheduled 2026-03-03).
- Confirm pilot customer list with Solutions/CS by 2026-03-08.
- Merge irrigation PR with detection notebook and export schema (PR 47 -> request review).
